title: What really makes a graph faster

questions.q: You read that a node makes graphs 3 times faster. What do you know?
options: What to try, not what you'll get
That it will be 3 times faster for you
That it only works on Linux
questions.answer: What to try, not what you'll get
questions.why: Someone else's card, model and steps. Measure on your own graph.
decode_tiled_ decodes three tile shapes and averages. Use it when the decode doesn't fit.

questions.q: By counting calls × cells, what does going from 1024 px to 512 px save?
questions.why: A quarter of the cells, at the same call count, leaves 25% of the baseline.

questions.q: When does cached conditioning help most?
options: Across restarts, or when a huge encoder is the problem
When the prompt changes each run
questions.answer: Across restarts, or when a huge encoder is the problem
questions.why: The node cache already covers repeats in one session. It doesn't touch sampling.

questions.q: Our first render took 66 s, and later ones 1.5 s. What does that measure?
options: Euler being slower than other samplers
questions.why: The first render of a model includes loading it. Leave it out.

options: Same seed, one change, first run dropped, median of three, and look at the picture
One run of each on different seeds
Your best time against someone's post
questions.answer: Same seed, one change, first run dropped, median of three, and look at the picture
questions.why: Every part removes a way of fooling yourself.
